reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports the formation of a ~400 nm amorphous-crystalline nanocomposite layer with ~10 nm Ag nanocrystals, a friction coefficient of ~0.09, and a wear rate reduction of up to two orders of magnitude in a (TiNbZr)75Ag25 alloy. However, the hypothesis proposes these outcomes at only 5 at% Ag, while the evidence is for 25 at% Ag, and the claimed 20% friction reduction and one-order-of-magnitude wear improvement are extrapolations not directly supported by the cited data.
premises: Ag doping promotes in situ formation of an amorphous-crystalline oxide nanocomposite surface layer during wear
The nanocomposite layer is ~400 nm thick with ~10 nm Ag nanocrystals embedded in an amorphous oxide matrix
This layer reduces friction coefficient to ~0.09 and wear rate by up to two orders of magnitude
The mechanism relies on positive mixing enthalpy between Ag and Nb driving Ag nanocrystal nucleation
The effect is demonstrated in a (TiNbZr)-based alloy system under ambient air wear conditions
